Trying to deactivate a supplement still in use by an active booking, tour, or custom tour offer returns "This supplement is used in active tour, booking or custom tour."
Uploaded images are checked for file size and image type; invalid ones are rejected.

permissions.fact: Creating, editing, categorizing, pricing, and translating supplements all require staff to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission.
Uploading or deleting a supplement image only requires being logged in.
Managing the supplement catalog from the platform's central administration console uses a separate system-level authorization, not a normal staff login.

field_meanings.fact: Name / Description — the display name and detail text for the add-on.
Price — the supplement's base price in the tenant's own currency, from which all other currency prices are derived.
Pricing Unit — how the supplement is charged: once per booking, per day, per week, or per night, each either flat or multiplied by passenger count.
Mandatory — whether the supplement must always be included wherever it's offered, with no option to remove it.
Contributes to Total — whether the supplement's price is counted in the overall total, even when it's still shown to the customer.
Complimentary — marks the supplement as free of charge.
Sales Cut-Off — an optional rule limiting how close to departure the supplement can still be sold.
Category — the catalog grouping this supplement belongs to, which can itself sit under a parent category.
Supplier — the external supplier who provides or fulfills this add-on, if any.
Tax Class — the tax rule applied to this supplement's price; defaults to "No VAT" if not set.
Supplement Group (Single/Multiple Choice, Required) — a cluster of related supplements presented together, either as a single choice or multiple choices, optionally required.
Translation (Name, Description) — the supplement's or category's content shown to customers in a specific language.

journeys.fact: To add a new add-on: staff enter its name, price, pricing unit, and category; the system fills in a default-language translation and prices in every supported currency automatically, without extra steps.
To organize the catalog: staff set up categories (optionally nested) before assigning supplements to them; a duplicate category name is rejected immediately.
To adjust pricing for a specific market: staff override the auto-converted price for one currency directly, without changing the supplement's base price.
To make a supplement available in more languages: staff add one translation per language; a language that isn't active can't be used for a translation.
To retire a supplement: staff deactivate it, which is blocked while it's still attached to any active booking, tour, or custom tour offer — those need to be resolved first.

side_effects.fact: A supplement's catalog entry is shared across features — it's referenced from Tours, Bookings, and Custom Tour Offers, which is exactly why deactivating an in-use supplement is blocked.
Turning on a new currency for the tenant automatically prices every active supplement in that currency.
A supplement's price calculation (for a given trip's dates and passenger count) is shared logic other features draw on when attaching a supplement to a booking.

features.name: Products
features.summary: Generic sellable products with categories, images, files and notes.

workflows.fact: Staff create a product with its name, supplier(s), location/address, and contact details.
Creating a product automatically creates a matching translation in the tenant's default language.
Staff organize a product into categories, each scoped to that one product rather than shared across the whole catalog.
Staff upload a gallery of images to a product, optionally marking one as the primary image, and add alt text for accessibility.
Staff upload a single representative image to a category.
Staff attach documents (contracts, spec sheets, etc.) to a product, giving each one a display name.
Staff add free-text internal notes to a product, shown newest first, each attributed to the staff member who wrote it.
Staff add translations of a product or category one language at a time.
Editing a product's name while working in a specific language updates that language's translation, not the original default-language name.
Staff deactivate a product or category as a separate action from editing its content.

rules.fact: A product or category can only have one translation per language — a duplicate is rejected.
Every new product and category automatically gets a translation created in the tenant's default language, with no separate step required.
A translation can only be added in a language that's currently active.
Attached files must be under 10 MB and one of a limited set of file types (images, PDF, plain text, Word documents).
A product's active/inactive status can only be changed through its dedicated status action, not through the general edit form.
Searching the product or category list matches either the base name or its translated name in whichever language is being viewed.

validations.fact: Changing a product's or category's status without specifying active/inactive returns "'is_active' field is required."
Adding a translation in an inactive language returns "Language is not active."
Adding a second translation for a language that already has one returns "A multilanguage entry for this product and language already exists." (or the equivalent for a category).
Requesting a product's translation without specifying which language returns "language_code query parameter or Accept-Language header is required."
Uploading a file of an unsupported type is rejected, naming which file types are actually allowed.
Uploading a file over 10 MB is rejected.
Attaching a file without giving it a name is rejected — a name is required alongside the file.

permissions.fact: Creating, editing, categorizing, uploading images/files, adding notes, and translating products all require staff to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission.

field_meanings.fact: Name / Description / Remarks — the product's display name, customer-facing description, and internal notes text (Remarks is separate from the internal Notes list).
Supplier Type / Supplier — the kind of vendor this product comes from, and the actual vendor(s) fulfilling it; a product can be linked to more than one supplier.
Contact Person Name / Email — the point of contact at the supplier or location for this product.
Location, Territory, Address — where the product is physically located or delivered from.
Map URL — a link to an external map pinpointing the product's location.
Image / Primary Image — a picture in the product's gallery, with one optionally marked as the main image.
File / File Name — a downloadable document attached to the product, such as a contract or spec sheet.
Note — a free-text internal comment about the product, visible only to staff.
Category — a grouping under one specific product, used to organize what's sellable under it; each category belongs to exactly one product.
Active/Inactive — whether the product or category is currently published, toggled only through its dedicated status action.

journeys.fact: To list a new product: staff enter its name, supplier(s), location, and contact details; a translation in the tenant's default language is created automatically.
To organize it: staff add categories scoped to that product, each with its own name, description, and image.
To flesh it out: staff upload a gallery of images (with one as the main image), attach relevant documents, and leave internal notes for other staff.
To support more markets: staff add a translation per additional language needed.
To take it offline: staff deactivate it as a distinct action from editing its content.

side_effects.fact: A product exists purely as a standalone catalog/directory entry — it does not attach to bookings, tours, hotels, yacht charters, or custom tour offers, and has no pricing or tax configuration of its own.

features.name: Payments
features.summary: Payment methods, transactions, settlements, OCR payment import, and provider integrations (AltaPay).

workflows.fact: A payment can be applied to a booking, a ResPay account, an invoice, or a gift card — each routed to its own handler, but all recorded as a Transaction.
A successful booking payment updates the booking's paid amount, cancels any pending payment-reminder emails for it, and finalizes the booking if it was still a draft.
Once a booking payment is processed, it can be pushed to the tenant's connected accounting system if that hasn't happened yet.

A refund creates its own transaction record (using a dedicated refund payment method) rather than reversing the original payment record, and reduces the booking's recorded paid amount by the refunded amount.
Staff can record a manual payment directly (e.g. bank transfer, cash) as an admin-only action, separate from the automated provider payment flows.

rules.fact: A refund can't be processed through a payment method that isn't configured for the tenant — except when the refund is being triggered automatically as part of cancelling a booking, which is allowed regardless.

Every transaction tracks both a payment status (pending/success/failed) and a separate settlement status, since a payment succeeding and that payment being settled/reconciled with accounting are tracked as two different states.

validations.fact: Attempting a refund through an unconfigured payment method is rejected with 'Payment Method is not configured.' (except for cancellation-triggered refunds).

permissions.fact: Viewing/managing transactions requires staff authentication plus Django model permissions.
Recording a manual payment is restricted to admin users specifically, not just any authenticated staff member.
A passenger can view their own transaction history (or, for staff impersonating a passenger, a read-only view of it); public payment status lookup requires no authentication at all.
Public-facing payment status information requires no authentication.

field_meanings.fact: A Transaction's amount is what the transaction covers; pending_amount tracks how much of it is still awaiting completion (relevant for payment methods that don't settle instantly).
A transaction can be linked to a booking, a ResPay account, a billing invoice, or a gift card — which one it's linked to determines what business impact processing it has.

journeys.fact: A customer pays for their booking online through one of the tenant's supported payment options; on success, the booking's balance updates immediately and any pending payment reminder for it is cancelled.
When a booking is cancelled, any refund owed is created and processed automatically as part of the cancellation, without a separate manual refund step.

side_effects.fact: Payments and refunds both interact with the tenant's connected accounting system, marking a transaction as sent once that sync succeeds.

features.name: Billing & Invoicing
features.summary: Billing lines and account invoices generated from bookings.

workflows.fact: A booking's charges (tour price, supplements, extras, fees) accumulate as Billing Lines, which get grouped onto an Account Invoice for that booking.

An invoice starts as a Draft and is editable in that state; issuing it locks it (no longer editable), assigns it a permanent invoice number and a payment reference number, and — if the tenant has accounting integration enabled — sends it there.
Issuing an invoice for a booking still in Quote status automatically accepts that quote as part of the same step.

An issued invoice can be voided (unlinking its billing lines and marking it void) or credited (generating a credit note that reverses its billing lines) — both only apply to invoices that are actually in Issued status.
Voiding an invoice that's already been booked in the connected accounting system is blocked, since undoing it there isn't possible from this side.

rules.fact: An invoice cannot be issued twice — issuing an already-issued invoice is rejected outright.
An invoice with no billing lines cannot be issued.
An invoice can only be voided if it's currently Issued, and only if it hasn't been paid or partially paid — a paid invoice must be credited, not voided.
An invoice can only be credited if it's currently Issued.
Every billing line carries its own VAT percentage and VAT amount, calculated per line rather than once for the whole invoice.

validations.fact: Issuing an already-issued invoice is rejected with 'Cannot issue an already issued invoice.'
Issuing an invoice with no billing lines is rejected with 'Cannot issue an invoice with no billing lines.'
Voiding a non-issued invoice is rejected with 'Cannot void a non-issued invoice.'; voiding a paid or partially-paid one is rejected with 'Cannot void a paid invoice.'
Voiding an invoice already booked in the connected accounting system is rejected with 'Cannot void an invoice that is already booked in the accounting service.'
Crediting a non-issued invoice is rejected with 'This invoice cannot be credited as it is not issued.'

permissions.fact: All invoice and billing-line operations (view, create, issue, void, credit, delete, download, email) require staff authentication.

field_meanings.fact: An invoice's status (Draft, Issued, Void) is separate from its payment status (Unpaid, Partially Paid, Paid) — an invoice can be Issued and still Unpaid, or Issued and fully Paid.

A billing line can belong to more than one kind of source (a booking's tour price, a supplement, an extra, a supplier charge) via a generic content-type link, letting one invoice combine charges from different parts of a booking.
An invoice is only editable while it's in Draft status — once issued, its content is locked.

journeys.fact: Staff review a booking's accumulated billing lines, generate a draft invoice, and issue it once it's correct — issuing locks the invoice, generates its final numbering, and (if enabled) pushes it to the connected accounting system.
If an issued invoice turns out to be wrong before any payment, staff void it; if it's already been paid, staff issue a credit note against it instead.

side_effects.fact: Issuing an invoice updates every billing line on it to reflect that it's now part of an issued invoice, and can trigger sending the invoice to the tenant's connected accounting system.
Voiding an invoice snapshots its billing lines onto the invoice record itself before unlinking them, preserving a record of what the invoice contained.
